content:
Tom Blomfield, the Monzo co-founder and one of the UK’s most high-profile technology entrepreneurs, has left his role at AI giant Anthropic after less than six months, according to several sources.

Blomfield announced he was joining Anthropic in July this year, saying he was taking a leave of absence from his role as a partner at Y Combinator, the San Francisco-based accelerator and investor, to join the compute team at Anthropic, which makes the Claude chatbot.

Blomfield posted on X at the time: “Powerful AI has the potential to improve the life of every human on Earth and, as we enter the early stages of recursive self-improvement, availability of compute becomes one of the most important issues to solve. I’m excited to get started.” 

In September, he posted on X: "Overall impression of @anthropicAI after 2 months; hyper-earnest group of meganerds who are very very focussed on ensuring this AI thing goes well for humans. It's not perfect by any means, but it has the most powerful sense of mission of any company I've ever encountered. Including @monzo, which I thought was an outlier."

The Monzo co-founder was working with Tom Brown, Anthropic co-founder and chief compute officer. It is not known why Blomfield has left Anthropic. Blomfield’s X profile still says he is a member of the technical staff at Anthropic, which recently undertook a blockbuster IPO.

Blomfield is most well known as the co-founder and CEO of digital bank Monzo,which launched in 2015 but he left in 2021 after earlier stepping down as CEO. He is also a prominent angel investor.

Anthropic declined to comment.
